approaches.name: A: Mirror java.rs/swift.rs with all five queries (recommended)
approaches.description: Add tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 (LANGUAGE_PHP entry point, not LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY) to workspace and core Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock; add languages/php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY and extract_inheritance (iterate children for base_clause and class_interface_clause); register php in EXTENSION_MAP, supported_languages(), get_language_info() and get_ts_language(); skip extract_function_name/find_method_for_receiver/find_receiver_type as the issue excludes them. Import capture uses namespace_use_clause with anchor so each imported name is one capture; the default arm of extract_imports_from_node stores the captured text as the module.

No edits outside languages/php.rs and registry files

cons: Import module names are raw clause text (no namespace split) unless shared import code is extended

approaches.description: Like A, but extend extract_imports_from_node in crates/aptu-coder-core/src/parser_elements.rs with a namespace_use_clause / qualified_name arm that splits on backslash into module and items, so imports read as module plus item rather than raw text.

cons: Touches shared import code used by Rust, Python and others; blast radius beyond PHP
Outside the issue's listed Scope (issue says handler, registry, tests, README)
Needs extra tests for every other language's import path

recommendation: Approach A. It matches the issue Scope (five constants, extract_inheritance, registry wiring, tests), mirrors java.rs and swift.rs, and every proposed query was run against the real grammar. Keep import output at clause level (anchored namespace_use_clause) and defer namespace splitting (C) to a follow-up since it touches shared code. Add php to supported_languages() explicitly; the CSS/YAML omission suggests the wiring checklist must be verified by a test that calls SemanticExtractor on a .php file.

ELEMENT_QUERY (verified to compile and capture against tree-sitter-php 0.25.2):
(function_definition
  name: (name) @func_name) @function
(method_declaration
  name: (name) @method_name) @function
(class_declaration
  name: (name) @class_name) @class
(interface_declaration
  name: (name) @interface_name) @class
(trait_declaration
  name: (name) @trait_name) @class
(enum_declaration
  name: (name) @enum_name) @class
inheritance_walk_citation: Source inspected: tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 (GitHub master php/grammar.js delegates to common/define-grammar.js, which matches the published crate copy; php/src/node-types.json identical to the crate copy). Walk for a class declaration: (1) class_declaration is `prec.right(seq(optional(field('attributes', attribute_list)), repeat(_modifier), keyword('class'), field('name', reserved('classes', name)), optional(base_clause), optional(class_interface_clause), field('body', declaration_list)))`. (2) The name is reached with child_by_field_name("name"); the body with child_by_field_name("body"). (3) base_clause is `seq(keyword('extends'), commaSep1($._name))` with NO field name, so it must be found by iterating children (child(i) / named_children) and matching kind()=="base_clause". Each named child of base_clause is one of name, qualified_name, relative_name (from hidden _name). Each becomes "extends <text>". (4) class_interface_clause is `seq(keyword('implements'), commaSep1($._name))`, also with NO field name; find by kind()=="class_interface_clause" and map each named child to "implements <text>". (5) Same clauses appear on interface_declaration (base_clause only, = interface extends list), enum_declaration (optional ': string|int' primitive_type, then optional class_interface_clause), and not on trait_declaration (no clause; returns []). Verified sexp for `<?php class Foo extends Bar implements A, B {}`: (class_declaration name: (name) (base_clause (name)) (class_interface_clause (name) (name)) body: (declaration_list)). Note: the element query captures interface/trait/enum nodes as @class too, so the handler receives those kinds and must not restrict itself to class_declaration. Qualified names keep their leading backslash in text (e.g. \Foo\Bar).
